role: independent fixed-commit Windows root-identity and lock-boundary auditor
card_sha: supplied in the single starter message after this card is committed
goal: At the exact review SHA, independently audit the Windows root-identity and lock boundary: path-to-physical-identity resolution, alias/junction handling, root lock acquisition and lifetime, poison/failure cleanup, and whether the allowed root-identity tests actually falsify the claimed guarantees. Identify up to five concrete actionable findings with exact file:line evidence, the necessary preconditions, and a falsifying test idea; or explicitly report no findings and static limits. Distinguish local Rust API facts from any unverified IPC or deployment assumption. Use small targeted GitHub reads. This is a static audit only: do not run a local CLI, perform Win11 tests, sign, or modify reviewed code.
success_criteria: One result-file commit on assigned_branch from base_sha naming review_sha, with findings or explicit no findings; Controller verifies a real CI run on the exact result commit with more than zero executed tests and checks main for unexpected commits.
stop_condition: Stop after one result commit. If a confirmed persistent GitHub permission or platform blockage prevents writing even the result file, stop with exact remote state. No chat follow-up.
economic_reason: A cross-file root-identity and lock-authority security audit at a fixed SHA would ordinarily use an Astra subagent (historical median about $4.1), clearly above estimated direct web overhead of $1.6-1.9; this task is self-contained, non-local, non-urgent, and GitHub-verifiable.
construction_rules: Before work read docs/governance/gpt-construction-window-rules.md sections 2, 3, 4, 5, 5a, 6, and 8. Sections 8a, 8b, and 9 are for long-running construction windows and do not apply to this one-off audit. Use small reads, make early durable GitHub progress, continue through ordinary tool/CI failures, and require real executed-test evidence. Ask no question in chat. If information is missing or a persistent permission/platform block is confirmed, write the blocker in result_path, commit if possible, and end.
remote_write_protocol: A failed GitHub write does not prove nothing landed or that permission is absent. First reread actual remote branch, commit, and file; if landed, continue without duplicate writes. If absent, retry after increasing intervals and identify the failing layer: ChatGPT action permission, GitHub App installation scope, selected repository, repository permission, ref API, or branch state. One 403 does not prove no write permission; 422 already exists may indicate a prior success. Never repeat a side-effecting write while remote state is unknown.
permission_boundary: Push only assigned_branch and only allowed_write_paths. Never push or merge main; do not publish, release, tag, access secrets, or sign. Do not claim project acceptance.
